definition: The percentage change in quantity bought for a 1% change in price. Above 1 (elastic), a price cut raises total spending; below 1 (inelastic), it lowers it.

A China-market version of NVIDIA's H100 (2023) with the same compute but cut-down NVLink bandwidth, designed to fit the October 2022 US export rules; it was itself restricted from November 2023. DeepSeek-V3 was trained on 2,048 of them.

A China-market Hopper GPU (2024) with much lower compute than the H100 but full HBM capacity, designed to fit the October 2023 export rules; it became subject to a US licence requirement in April 2025.
Training a smaller 'student' model to imitate a larger 'teacher' model's outputs. It transfers much of the teacher's ability at a fraction of the serving cost.

DeepSeek's pipeline-parallel schedule that overlaps the forward and backward computation of different micro-batches with the expert-parallel all-to-all communication, hiding most of the network time on bandwidth-limited H800 clusters.

A sudden fall in the compute (and so cost) needed per unit of AI output, from a new model architecture, training method or software. Whether it lowers or raises total compute spend depends on the price elasticity of demand.
